arxiv-2606-16107: Image compression usually locks you into one quality level, but a variable-rate codec lets you dial quality up or down. This paper builds one using low-rank adaptation (LoRA) trained progressively — small, efficient updates added step by step. The result is a flexible deep-learning compressor for engineers who need adjustable quality on the fly.
arxiv-2606-16207: Why is there stuff but near-zero anti-stuff, and why do ghost bits (neutrinos) weigh so slight? This bit-physics paper floats one frame that ties both riddles: an S4 shape-rule, a dark birth-route for neutrino heft, and a tilt that left more stuff than anti-stuff. For deep-theory fans.
arxiv-2606-16407: Language models sometimes swap pronouns mid-story, breaking who-did-what. This paper digs into the mechanisms behind "pronoun fidelity" in LLMs — how models track who "he," "she," or "they" refers to across long texts. The mechanistic analysis helps researchers understand and fix reference-tracking failures.
arxiv-2606-16507: Galaxies wear their history in their spiral arms and bars. This astronomy paper uses deep learning to find those structures in 600,000 galaxies from the DESI survey — a catalog far too large for humans to inspect. The resulting map of galactic shapes fuels studies of how galaxies grow and evolve.
arxiv-2606-16707: AI assistants that know you need memory — but memory is usually a messy pile of notes. 'User as Code' turns your profile into executable memory: code the agent can actually run to recall who you are. The paper presents the idea for researchers building personalized agents.
arxiv-2606-16807: Children learn words by hearing them while seeing the world. This paper connects speech to words through images: training AI to link spoken sounds with written words via pictures. It is for speech researchers building systems that learn language the way kids do.
arxiv-2606-16907: GPUs differ — training across mixed GPUs wastes time. Tangram hides GPU heterogeneity for efficient LLM parallelization: it balances the load so no GPU idles. It is for systems engineers training big models on mixed hardware. Mixed chips, smooth and fast training.
